label: Lake
_model: Wild kernel in still water. Where the river wants movement, the lake wants none: to be left flat, to be looked into, to keep what is under it exactly as it was, and to be a little bigger every year. Claimants are the water's own names for itself.

appetites.purpose: the surface would never move again

appeasement.move: stand at the edge and put nothing at all into the water

appetites.want: that everything should stop and look into it

appeasement.move: look into the water, properly, and do not look away first

appetites.want: that what is under it should be remembered as it was
appetites.purpose: nothing down there would ever be given up

appeasement.move: name something that is under the water, and where it stood

appetites.want: to be a little wider every year
appetites.purpose: it would go on getting bigger forever
appetites.asks: "Where do you think my edge is?"

appeasement.move: let the water have one thing it is reaching for

factions.name: the Still

factions.name: the fishers

factions.name: what lives in the weed beds

factions.name: what is in the reflection

triggerGlossary.announced: came down to the shore in the open and stood where the water could see you
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: reflected twice, from two different points of the shore
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice over flat water, which carries to the far bank

skirmish.line: 3 Giant Rats in the reed bed
skirmish.avoid: they will not come out of the reeds onto open shingle

fight.line: 3 Ghouls out of the weed beds

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: free Called Shot to freeze on a hit; they come up without a sound

fight.avoid: they will not leave the water — get clear of the shallows and they stop at the line

battle.line: 1 Troll in the shallows and 2 Ghouls

foes.name: Troll
foes.note: REGENERATES 2 Grit a round unless the wound was burnt; wet, so fire is hard here

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: free Called Shot to freeze on a hit

battle.harmedBy: anything, but the Troll only stays down if fire touches it, and everything here is wet
battle.avoid: it will not go into deep water; the boat is safe from it and the shore is not

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith standing on the water, 1 Troll and 4 Ghouls

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit; it does not break the surface

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest, fire for the Troll and it is wet
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open

stillness.dangerLine: the water has been flat for a long time and it notices everything that touches it

decisions.cue: a surface with one ring on it, spreading, from nothing that fell
decisions.cost: something came up, or something is about to

resolve.success: you read the ring and know what is under it and how far off
resolve.failure: you throw something to see and the water counts that against you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: back off the shore; whatever made the ring surfaces behind you later

decisions.cue: a slipway with the water lying against it and not lapping at all
decisions.cost: putting a boat in will be the loudest thing that has happened here in years

resolve.success: you launch without a sound and the water lets the boat cross the middle
resolve.failure: you put it in badly and the whole lake registers it, at once: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: stay ashore; the far side is a full day round, and it gets dark

decisions.cue: a shore raked over recently to hide what came out of the water
decisions.cost: somebody is tidying up after it

resolve.success: you read what was raked over and know what comes ashore and how often
resolve.failure: you rake it again yourself and are taken for the one who has been doing it
resolve.orElse: leave the shingle; you camp on it not knowing what uses it

decisions.cue: boats swamped at their moorings on a night with no wind at all
decisions.cost: the water came up into them deliberately

resolve.success: you find the one boat it left alone and understand why, and can use it
resolve.failure: you bail one out and it is swamped again with you in it
resolve.orElse: take no boat; every route is round the shore, and the shore is long

decisions.cue: a stone in your hand and a flat water in front of you
decisions.cost: throwing it is the most natural thing in the world

resolve.success: you put the stone down and the water is pleased, and shows you something
resolve.failure: you throw it, of course you do, and the rings do not stop spreading
resolve.orElse: throw it deliberately, as a challenge; it answers, and it is bigger than you

decisions.cue: fine shingle laid so nothing can roll into the water
decisions.cost: somebody made this shore so that nothing would ever disturb it

resolve.failure: you walk it carelessly and send a stone in, and the flatness ends
resolve.orElse: go along the bank above the shingle, costing a Turn in the alder carr

situations.doing: lying dead flat while the wind moves everything on the bank
situations.onArrival: a single ring spreads on it from nothing at all
situations.because: it has been flat a long time and something has just moved under it
situations.offer: put nothing in and stand still, and it will show you what is down there

situations.doing: holding an oar above the water without putting it in
situations.onArrival: he asks whether you would mind waiting a moment
situations.because: he has not broken the surface in years and it is how he still has a boat
situations.offer: wait with him and he will row you anywhere on it

situations.doing: standing waist-deep with the water flat against it
situations.onArrival: it does not ripple and neither does the water
situations.because: it went in without a sound and the lake approved
situations.offer: go in as quietly and it will take you across the middle

situations.doing: lying drawn up dry on a slipway with the water against it
situations.onArrival: the water does not lap at the slip and the boat is warm
situations.because: boats go in silently here or not at all
situations.offer: launch it without a sound and the middle water opens to you

situations.doing: lying raked flat with something dragged across it and smoothed over
situations.onArrival: the rake marks stop halfway and are not resumed
situations.because: somebody tidies up after what comes out and stopped mid-job
situations.offer: finish the raking and whatever comes ashore treats you as its keeper

situations.doing: filling the whole middle of the lake with a flatness you can see from the bank
situations.onArrival: it goes flatter, visibly, as you come down to the water
situations.because: it wants no ring on it at all, ever
situations.offer: give it a still hour and it will let you cross without a boat

temptations.cue: the stone that made no ring
temptations.benefit: once, do a thing without being noticed
temptations.standingDrawback: the lake watches you continuously instead

temptations.cue: a muffled oar
temptations.benefit: cross the water without breaking it
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot move fast on the water at all

temptations.cue: a handful of the fine shingle
temptations.benefit: once, make ground that does not give you away
temptations.standingDrawback: it gives away whoever crosses it after you

temptations.cue: the shore-keeper's rake
temptations.benefit: once, hide that something came out

temptations.cue: a knack for reading rings
temptations.benefit: know what is under the surface near you
temptations.standingDrawback: you know before you can do anything about it

mirror.dangerLine: the water shows you what is there, and lately it has been showing a little more than that

decisions.cue: a reflection that comes a half-second behind you
decisions.cost: the delay is small and it is getting smaller

resolve.success: you catch the delay and can tell reflection from thing for the rest of the delve
resolve.failure: you watch it until it catches up and it is level with you now: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: stop looking in; you cannot tell, later, which of two things is which

decisions.cue: a still panel of water in the reeds at exactly face height
decisions.cost: it is at that height because that is where faces go

resolve.success: you look in deliberately and do not look away first, and it yields something true
resolve.failure: you look and look away, and it keeps the part you did not finish looking at
resolve.orElse: do not look; the water asks you again in every area after this

decisions.cue: a reflection showing somebody standing beside you who is not
decisions.cost: the extra figure is doing what you do, nearly

resolve.success: you speak to it rather than about it and it answers, and it is useful
resolve.failure: you turn to look and it is behind you now instead of beside you
resolve.orElse: ignore it entirely; it walks with the party from here and nobody says so

decisions.cue: reeds cut down the whole length of a shore so nothing reflects
decisions.cost: somebody stopped this water being able to show anything

resolve.success: you find who cut them and what they were stopping being seen
resolve.failure: you clear a panel to look and it shows you what they were preventing
resolve.orElse: leave the shore bare; you never get a straight look at anything here

decisions.cue: a surface showing a village that is not on the bank

resolve.orElse: look away; you come to the ending without knowing what was drowned

decisions.cue: a piece of the surface that has stayed hard, lying on the shingle
decisions.cost: the water shed a bit of itself and it is still reflecting

resolve.success: you take it and can see what is actually in front of you, always
resolve.failure: you look into it too long and what is in it is looking back, from close

situations.doing: standing in the water beside yours and copying you a half-second late
situations.onArrival: it raises a hand slightly before you decide to
situations.because: the lake shows what is there and it has been embellishing
situations.offer: greet it rather than turn round, and it will show you what is under the water

situations.doing: standing at the water's edge looking at its own reflection
situations.onArrival: it asks you whether that looks like it
situations.because: it went in looking at itself and cannot stop
situations.offer: tell it the truth and it will let you look in safely, once

situations.doing: cutting the last reeds along a shore that is already bare
situations.onArrival: he asks whether you have looked in yet
situations.because: he has been stopping the water reflecting anything for years
situations.offer: ask him why and he will tell you exactly what the lake shows

situations.doing: lying in the reeds at exactly the height of a face
situations.onArrival: the reeds around it are pressed back at shoulder width
situations.because: everyone who passes looks in here
situations.offer: look in and do not look away, and the water gives you something true

situations.doing: showing under the surface with the lanes and the roofs clear
situations.onArrival: a light goes on in one of the reflected windows
situations.because: it shows what was there before the water rose
situations.offer: name a building aloud and the water will give up what is in it

situations.doing: standing in the reflection of the bank you are on, facing out
situations.onArrival: she is not standing on the bank itself
situations.because: she is on the other side of the surface, doing what you do
situations.offer: match her, exactly, and she will let you through to what is under

temptations.cue: the piece of surface that stayed hard

temptations.cue: a knowledge of the face-height panels

decisions.cue: a steeple showing above the water with the weathercock just clear
decisions.cost: the tower is enterable at this level and will not be for long

resolve.success: you get into the tower and the bell is there, and it can still be rung
resolve.failure: you go in on a falling level and the water comes back over the door
resolve.orElse: stay off it; the bell stays down there and the ending has no voice

decisions.cue: a bell heard from the bank on a day that is not the turn of the year
decisions.cost: something is ringing it, or something wants it rung

resolve.success: you answer the bell properly and the drowned parish receives you as visitors
resolve.failure: you row out to it and the ringing stops while you are over the tower
resolve.orElse: ignore it; it rings every area from here, closer each time

decisions.cue: a road going into the water with fresh tracks on it
decisions.cost: something has been using the road, in or out

resolve.success: you read the tracks and know which way and how recently, and can be elsewhere
resolve.failure: you follow them in and the road goes on down for a long way
resolve.orElse: take the shore path; it costs a Turn and passes the weed beds

decisions.cue: a village thirty feet down with the doors standing open
decisions.cost: open doors mean they left, or mean something got in

resolve.success: you work out which and know what is down there before you have to meet it
resolve.failure: you go down to look and one of the doors closes above you
resolve.orElse: stay on the surface; you meet what is in the village without warning

decisions.cue: stone robbed off the top courses of the drowned steeple
decisions.cost: somebody has been taking the church for building

resolve.success: you find where the stone went and it is standing in something you will visit
resolve.failure: you take a course yourself and the parish notices immediately
resolve.orElse: leave it; the theft is unacknowledged and the parish blames whoever comes

decisions.cue: a list of the parish as it was, house by house, in a dry hand
decisions.cost: the list is the whole memory of the place

resolve.success: you read it and can name anything down there, which is the appeasement in your hand
resolve.failure: you take it away and the parish loses the last record of itself
resolve.orElse: leave it; you go to the ending unable to name a single one of them

situations.doing: standing out of flat water with the weathercock just clear
situations.onArrival: the vane turns although there is no wind on the water
situations.because: the parish is down there and the tower is how you reach it
situations.offer: go in at the belfry window and the bell will answer to you

situations.doing: standing in a doorway thirty feet down, quite visible
situations.onArrival: it lifts a hand as your shadow crosses the water above
situations.because: it is at its own front door and has not been told
situations.offer: name its house aloud and it will open every door down there

situations.doing: landing dressed stone off a boat at a slipway
situations.onArrival: he asks whether you are here about the church
situations.because: he has been taking the steeple down a course at a time
situations.offer: tell him to stop and the parish will treat you as its advocate

situations.doing: sounding under the water on a day that is not the turn of the year
situations.onArrival: the sound arrives at the bank a moment after the water moves
situations.because: it is rung at the turn of the year and something has rung it early
situations.offer: answer it from the shore and the drowned parish comes up to talk

situations.doing: running down into the water with tracks on it going both ways
situations.onArrival: the tracks below the waterline are as fresh as the ones above
situations.because: the road went to the village and it still goes there
situations.offer: walk it in and the water lets you down as far as the crossroads

situations.doing: standing in its lanes under thirty feet of still water
situations.onArrival: every face down there turns up toward the boat at once
situations.because: they are kept as they were and would like to be remembered so
situations.offer: read them their own names and they will give you anything they have

temptations.cue: the bell out of the steeple

temptations.cue: a dressed stone off the church

decisions.cue: a level post with the water standing at the newest mark
decisions.cost: cutting a new mark records the rise; pulling the post denies it

resolve.success: you cut the year honestly and the water is satisfied to be measured, and eases
resolve.failure: you pull the post up and the water comes to where the post was: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it; the rise is unrecorded and nobody downstream is warned

decisions.cue: a marker stone set at last year's edge, now standing in water
decisions.cost: the stones say how fast, if you can find enough of them

resolve.success: you find the run of stones and know exactly how fast it is coming and when it reaches you
resolve.failure: you move one to where you would rather it were and the water follows it
resolve.orElse: ignore the stones; you camp somewhere that is under water by morning

decisions.cue: a drainage cut with the water sitting level in it and not draining
decisions.cost: the cut works and the lake is refusing to use it

resolve.success: you find the blockage and the cut runs, and one field comes back out of the water
resolve.failure: you deepen it and the lake comes up the cut instead, faster
resolve.orElse: fill the cut in; the lake is pleased and everything low is lost

decisions.cue: three old waterlines showing on a shore above the present one
decisions.cost: the lines are not evenly spaced and the gaps are the point

resolve.success: you read the spacing and know when it rose fastest, and what happened that year
resolve.failure: you read them wrong and are confident about a shore that is not safe
resolve.orElse: leave the shore; you have no idea how quickly this can move

decisions.cue: a village street with water standing in the doorways, ankle deep
decisions.cost: people are still living in some of these houses

resolve.success: you get the last of them out and they know every drain, cut and sluice here
resolve.failure: you go through and leave them, and they are part of the water by the ending
resolve.orElse: go round; the street is under to the sill by the time you come back

decisions.cue: dead trees standing a long way out in the shallows
decisions.cost: the water came up around them and they took years to die

resolve.success: you count the rings on a fallen one and know how long this has been happening
resolve.failure: you take one for a raft and the lake takes exception to being crossed on itself
resolve.orElse: leave them; you have no idea how old this appetite is

situations.doing: standing in water with every year cut into it and the newest mark under
situations.onArrival: the water is exactly at the top cut and is not moving
situations.because: the level is read each spring and the reading stopped
situations.offer: cut this year's mark and the water will not come further while you are here

situations.doing: digging a cut that is already full of level water
situations.onArrival: she asks whether it looks like it is running to you

situations.offer: tell her the truth and she will show you every low place here

situations.doing: standing in a doorway with water to its knees, keeping house
situations.onArrival: it apologises for the state of the floor
situations.because: the water rose over it and it has not accepted that it has
situations.offer: help it bail and it will tell you how far this water means to come

situations.onArrival: the nearest one is dry and the next one is not
situations.because: a stone is set at the edge each year and the line goes out a long way
situations.offer: set a stone at today's edge and the lake will stop at it for the delve

situations.doing: standing far out in the shallows with the bark long gone
situations.onArrival: the water around their roots is warmer than the rest

situations.onArrival: the water is a hand's width higher on the shingle than your first look

situations.offer: give it one thing it is reaching for and it will leave the rest
